topic: Sharp nested-survivor capacity for simultaneous TV-SACE and RM-SACE surfaces. Fix finite X, conditional exchangeability with treatment overlap, independent administrative censoring with at-risk probability bounded below through the full analysis horizon tau, semicompeting-risk order R(z)<D(z) for finite R(z), terminal-survival monotonicity D(1)>=D(0), bounded-Lipschitz finite-part event densities, and positive always-survivor mass on the target index set. Prove that the standardized compatible surface is exactly the image of conditional couplings nu_x=law(D(0),R(1)|X=x) satisfying all readmission-specific survivor-dominance inequalities. Give measurable full-law lifts, O(m^2) finite-grid chain flows and support duals, fixed-cohort cut formulas with common CDF extremizers and sharp RM integration, strict cross-cohort support examples, continuous support convergence, observable censoring-moment finite-sample outer sets, and multiplier bands on regular compact regions. Consumer: Comment et al., Biometrical Journal 2025, subject to follow-up, coding, monotonicity and covariate audits. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Conditional stochastic-order and quantile-lift derivations yield the iff projection; integer matching and suffix cuts yield the chain flow and common fixed-cohort extrema. A smooth three-horizon law has signed support [-1/20,1/4] versus rectangular [-3/20,7/20]; a five-level case has jointly attained prefix intervals [0,.09], [0,.19], [.11,.31]. Full-versus-projected LP checks agreed numerically, and full-horizon follow-up distinguishes the prior 0.6-versus-1 censoring counterexample. Observable at-risk/completion moment brackets plus Hoeffding regions give outer containment at changing faces. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the joint marked-product-limit/IPCW functional CLT and estimated-censoring expansion through tau, then compose it with the unique-cut derivative for consistent simultaneous multiplier bands with negligible grid bias. EARLY KILL TEST: Recompute the five-level full-law and projected-flow problem at gamma=.4, requiring all event-set cuts, prefix extrema [0,.09], [0,.19], [.11,.31], guard containment, and distinct .2-versus-0 observed death cells; any failure stops continuous inference. open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the sharp joint identified set of standardized TV-SACE and RM-SACE surfaces over all readmission and survivor horizons under terminal-survival monotonicity and every readmission-specific survivor-dominance restriction.

source_refs.claim: Comment et al. define two-index TV-SACE and its RM-SACE integral but address the unidentified principal-stratum law through a parametric Bayesian frailty model.
source_refs.author: Comment, Mealli, Haneuse, and Zigler

source_refs.claim: Yang and Ding sharpen scalar SACE bounds using survival histories and ranked-average-score restrictions, while indexing the latent joint survival law by a copula sensitivity parameter.
source_refs.author: Yang and Ding

source_refs.claim: Nevo and Gorfine derive partial-identification bounds for semi-competing-risk effects using a single population stratification rather than nested time-varying always-survivor cohorts.
source_refs.author: Nevo and Gorfine

open_problems.why_unsolved: Observed treatment arms identify relevant marginal event and death laws but not the cross-world coupling assigning treated readmission times to control survival times. Terminal monotonicity constrains the death-time coupling, while survivor dominance at each readmission threshold constrains a different nested section. Existing snapshot bounds optimize individual contrasts, and the Bayesian TV-SACE analysis closes the latent joint law parametrically; neither establishes that one conditional coupling generates every simultaneously compatible TV/RM surface or that every feasible coupling admits a measurable full potential-outcome lift.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if theorem representing the complete standardized TV-SACE/RM-SACE identified set as the image of measurable conditional couplings satisfying all indexed survivor-dominance inequalities, with a measurable full-law lifting theorem and sharp TV-to-RM integration.

writing_exemplar.why: Its clinical motivation, nested always-survivor cohorts, and joint TV-SACE/RM-SACE formulation provide the destination framing.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Death truncates readmission -> ordinary hazard contrasts condition on a post-treatment event -> principal strata define survivor effects -> the full TV-SACE/RM-SACE surface requires a sharp nonparametric compatibility analysis

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the equivalence between stochastic-order inequalities and order-supported couplings, including its separating-support-function proof.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The indexed survivor-dominance inequalities are intended to be exactly the feasibility conditions for a constrained conditional coupling.

method_exemplars.technique: Use measure-valued linear programming and random-set duality to prove sharpness for functionals of an unidentified joint potential-outcome distribution.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The TV/RM surface consists of linear functionals of a latent cross-world law subject to observed-marginal and order restrictions.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt randomly perturbed linear-program values and generic-basis stability to estimate support endpoints and conduct valid inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Finite-grid support functions of the compatible surface are LP values, although censoring and continuum indexing require new limit theory.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether the finite-grid nested-survivor coupling problem has an exact quadratic-size chain-flow representation with complete event-set cuts, support-function duals, and common extremizers across all readmission thresholds within a fixed survivor cohort.

source_refs.claim: Strassen characterizes order-supported couplings through inequalities over increasing sets but does not derive the nested-SACE chain reduction.
source_refs.author: Strassen

source_refs.claim: Russell gives generic LP methods for sharp bounds on functionals of joint potential-outcome laws without exploiting nested survivor structure.
source_refs.author: Russell

source_refs.claim: Ober-Reynolds characterizes sharp joint-potential-outcome bounds as optimal-transport values and estimates them through the dual, but does not impose readmission-indexed survivor dominance.
source_refs.author: Ober-Reynolds

open_problems.why_unsolved: Generic transport and linear-program formulations retain a full coupling table and do not show whether ordered death and readmission times collapse to a chain network. The literature scan found no treatment of nested survivor cuts or proof that one conditional CDF extremizer jointly attains all prefix objectives for a fixed cohort. The first missing proof step is a refinement of generic separation into a max-flow/min-cut equivalence whose complete cut family respects both semicompeting-risk support and survivor-threshold nesting.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-grid theorem giving an O(m^2)-size flow exactly equivalent to feasible full laws, a complete support dual and fixed-cohort cut formula with jointly attaining CDF extremizers, and Hausdorff convergence of grid support functions and RM integrals to their continuous-support counterparts.

writing_exemplar.why: Its progression from unidentified joint distributions to sharp computational bounds closely frames why an exact structural reduction matters.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Causal functionals depend on an unobserved joint law -> compatible laws form a linear program -> generic computation hides structure and scales poorly -> nested survivor restrictions may yield an exact chain-flow characterization

method_exemplars.technique: Specialize increasing-set coupling inequalities to suffix and event-set cuts, then prove sufficiency by a finite transportation construction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired flow conditions form a structured finite-poset version of Strassen's coupling criterion.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over primal measure LPs, support-function duality, and sharpness by measurable selection while replacing the generic grid LP with a nested chain network.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems optimize linear causal functionals over latent joint laws, but the destination requires an analytic sparse reduction and common extrema.

method_exemplars.technique: Use perturbations of LP values and active-basis stability to estimate support endpoints and obtain uniformly valid outer inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed support dual is a family of linear-program value functions.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish simultaneous multiplier bands for regular compact regions of the sharp TV-SACE and RM-SACE bound surfaces when marked event, death, and censoring laws are jointly estimated through the full horizon.

source_refs.author: Comment, Mealli, Haneuse, and Zigler

source_refs.author: Bluhmki, Dobler, Beyersmann, and Pauly

source_refs.claim: Fang and Santos show that ordinary bootstrap inference generally fails for merely directionally differentiable maps and provide derivative-based valid resampling.
source_refs.author: Fang and Santos

source_refs.excerpt: The load-bearing O_P(a_K) total-variation bound is an estimator-side restriction

open_problems.why_unsolved: Survival-process bootstrap theory handles smooth Nelson-Aalen or product-integral functionals before optimization, while directional-delta results assume an established primitive functional CLT. The prior CausalSmith review independently identifies the danger of imposing an abstract total-variation learner rate without primitive conditions that attain it. Here the primitive vector jointly contains marked recurrent-event, terminal-event, and estimated-censoring components, after which a cut or LP value map changes optimizer at ties. The missing composition requires a full-horizon estimated-censoring influence expansion, checkable entropy or cross-fitting conditions for uniform product-rate remainders, unique-cut separation on regular regions, and grid error negligible relative to n^{-1/2}.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving primitive learner and at-risk conditions for a joint asymptotic-linear expansion and functional CLT, Hadamard differentiation of unique-cut endpoints, and conditional multiplier convergence in ℓ∞ of a compact two-horizon region, yielding consistent simultaneous TV-SACE/RM-SACE bands with negligible grid bias.

writing_exemplar.why: It explains why clinically meaningful conclusions concern complete TV/RM surfaces rather than isolated horizons.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Clinical benefit accumulates over readmission time -> always-survivor cohorts vary with survival horizon -> pointwise intervals do not protect surface-level conclusions -> sharp nonparametric surfaces require simultaneous bands

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the multivariate counting-process martingale representation and increment-level multiplier proof for censored Nelson-Aalen processes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The SACE primitive moments are jointly marked event and death processes under right censoring and need process-level covariance preservation.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply the directional delta method and bootstrap an estimated directional derivative instead of directly bootstrapping the nonsmooth bound map.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A sharp endpoint is a max/min value and becomes only directionally differentiable when multiple cuts are active.

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer the uniform value-function resampling argument and chain rule for supremum-norm statistics indexed by a continuum.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired bound surface is an optimized value function indexed jointly by readmission and survivor horizons.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct honest finite-sample outer confidence sets for finite-grid TV-SACE/RM-SACE surfaces by propagating joint observable right-censoring moment regions through every changing face of the compatible-coupling polytope.

source_refs.claim: Goldberg derives data-dependent and uniform Hoeffding- and Bernstein-type inequalities for IPCW estimators under right censoring.
source_refs.author: Goldberg

source_refs.claim: Bitouze, Laurent, and Massart prove a DKW-type exponential inequality for the Kaplan-Meier distribution estimator.
source_refs.author: Bitouze, Laurent, and Massart

source_refs.claim: Cho and Russell obtain uniformly valid inference for linearly set-identified functionals through perturbed LP values, but their result is asymptotic and does not address censored event-process moments.
source_refs.author: Cho and Russell

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing exponential inequalities control an individual Kaplan-Meier curve or IPCW average, whereas LP procedures control optimized values asymptotically. The same estimated censoring survival enters many event and death cells here, so independent cellwise intervals discard dependence and need not form one jointly feasible moment region. What remains is a simultaneous observable-moment region with random denominators controlled by the at-risk lower bound, together with a proof that propagation through every possible active polytope face contains the true sharp surface.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A nonasymptotic theorem constructing a computable random outer set that contains the complete finite-grid sharp TV-SACE/RM-SACE surface with probability at least 1-alpha uniformly over the stated censoring and overlap class, plus a continuous-support extension with an explicit mesh remainder.

writing_exemplar.why: Its surface-valued clinical target explains why uncertainty must cover all compatible horizons instead of a selected scalar contrast.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: TV/RM effects depend on clinically selected horizons -> their principal-stratum law is partially identified -> sampling and censoring add uncertainty -> an honest outer set must cover the full compatible surface

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt data-dependent IPCW Hoeffding and Bernstein bounds while retaining the censoring-survival denominator in the finite-sample event.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Observable compatible-law constraints are censoring-weighted bounded moments, matching the primitive object controlled by Goldberg.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the Duhamel-equation reduction of Kaplan-Meier error to empirical-process deviations to obtain a simultaneous censoring-law guard.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Uniform control of estimated censoring through tau is needed before IPCW moment inequalities can be finite-sample honest.

method_exemplars.technique: Propagate a joint confidence region for linear moments through perturbed primal and dual LPs while accounting for active-face changes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The causal target is the image of a polytope defined by linear moment inequalities, but its primitive region is censoring-aware and finite-sample.

open_problems.open_problem: Extend sharp nested-survivor capacity from a first nonterminal event to a recurrent-readmission counting process with distinct cumulative-count and always-survivor horizons.

source_refs.claim: Lyu et al. define a principal-stratum effect for recurrent events truncated by death using a parametric Bayesian frailty model and focus on equal count and survival horizons.
source_refs.author: Lyu, Bornkamp, Mueller-Velten, and Schmidli

source_refs.claim: Comment et al. develop TV-SACE and RM-SACE for a nonrecurrent nonterminal event.
source_refs.author: Comment, Mealli, Haneuse, and Zigler

source_refs.claim: Janvin et al. formalize causal estimands for recurrent events with competing death, principally targeting total, direct, and separable effects rather than sharp always-survivor bounds.
source_refs.author: Janvin, Young, Ryalen, and Stensrud

open_problems.why_unsolved: The recurrent-event principal-stratum literature supplies a destination estimand but closes its cross-world law through a parametric shared-frailty model, while nonparametric recurrent-event work targets different whole-population or separable effects. A first-event dominance proof uses nested indicators of R(z)≤r; replacing R by a counting path requires restrictions over increasing cylinder sets, and a finite-grid flow must track count increments as well as death order. The targeted scan located no sharp coupling characterization for this recurrent always-survivor surface.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp identified-set theorem for E[N(1,r)-N(0,r) given D(1)>t and D(0)>t] as the image of path/death couplings satisfying explicit cylinder-set dominance inequalities, with a finite-grid flow characterization or a regime-specific counterexample showing when the first-event chain reduction fails.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the clinically native recurrent-hospitalization estimand and why death makes its principal stratum latent.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Hospitalizations recur -> death terminates the recurrence process -> marginal rate contrasts mix survival with recurrence -> an always-survivor cumulative-count surface needs sharp nonparametric bounds

method_exemplars.technique: Lift a discretized recurrent-count path to finite random-set support and optimize cumulative-count functionals over compatible joint laws.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After discretization, the destination parameter is linear in a latent joint law, matching Russell's sharp random-set LP framework.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the discrete-time counting-process representation and proof of convergence to continuous-time causal functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the path-space causal bookkeeping and fine-grid limit needed after replacing one readmission time by a recurrent process.

method_exemplars.technique: Use counting-process multiplier increments and the corresponding martingale conditional-CLT proof for simultaneous resampling.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Recurrent-event paths have multiple jumps per subject and require preservation of their process-level covariance structure.

literature_map:
1. Comment, Mealli, Haneuse, and Zigler (2025, Biometrical Journal, arXiv:1902.09304) introduce TV-SACE and RM-SACE for semi-competing risks but use a partially identified parametric Bayesian frailty likelihood.
2. Zhang and Rubin (2003, JEBS, doi:10.3102/10769986028004353) establish foundational scalar principal-stratum bounds for outcomes truncated by death.
3. Long and Hudgens (2013, Biometrics, doi:10.1111/biom.12103) show categorical covariate adjustment can strictly sharpen principal-effect bounds but remain at a scalar outcome horizon.
4. Yang and Ding (2018, Biometrics, arXiv:1803.02024) exploit detailed survival histories and ranked-average-score restrictions while indexing cross-world survival dependence by a copula parameter.
5. Wang, Zhou, and Richardson (2017, Biometrika, doi:10.1093/biomet/asx034) identify and estimate SACE under additional latent-stratum structure, underscoring that the observed law alone does not recover it.
6. Nevo and Gorfine (2022, Biostatistics, arXiv:2010.04485) derive semi-competing-risk partial-identification bounds using one population stratification, contrasting with nested TV-SACE cohorts.
7. Lyu, Bornkamp, Mueller-Velten, and Schmidli (2023, Biometrics, doi:10.1111/biom.13831) formulate recurrent-event principal-stratum effects but use parametric Bayesian joint frailty models and emphasize equal horizons.
8. Janvin, Young, Ryalen, and Stensrud (2024, Lifetime Data Analysis, arXiv:2202.08500) formalize recurrent/competing-event estimands and fine-grid limits, mostly for total, direct, and separable effects.
9. Strassen (1965, Annals of Mathematical Statistics, doi:10.1214/aoms/1177700153) links stochastic-order inequalities to order-supported couplings.
10. Russell (2021, JBES, doi:10.1080/07350015.2019.1684300) gives sharp LP/random-set bounds for latent joint potential-outcome laws but no nested-survivor chain reduction.
11. Ober-Reynolds (2023, arXiv:2311.09435) casts sharp joint-potential-outcome bounds as optimal-transport values and develops dual estimators.
12. Cho and Russell (2024, JBES, arXiv:1810.03180) bootstrap perturbed LP values for uniformly valid inference on linearly set-identified functionals.
13. Bluhmki, Dobler, Beyersmann, and Pauly (2019, Lifetime Data Analysis, doi:10.1007/s10985-018-9423-x) prove a multivariate Nelson-Aalen wild-bootstrap CLT and simultaneous bands under censoring.
14. Fang and Santos (2019, Review of Economic Studies, arXiv:1404.3763) and Firpo, Galvao, and Parker (2023, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:1911.10215) supply directional-delta and uniform optimized-value inference but presuppose a primitive FCLT.
15. Bitouze, Laurent, and Massart (1999, AIHP, doi:10.1016/S0246-0203(99)00112-0) and Goldberg (2019, arXiv:1903.01991) provide Kaplan-Meier/IPCW concentration, leaving its joint propagation through changing SACE-polytope faces unresolved.
